en: The Thousand-Name Hymn of the Auspicious Āñjaneya
The sages said:
O scorcher of foes, what is that mantra and what is its meditation? Tell us that according to the truth; having drunk the nectar-essence of your stories, we are not yet satiated.
Vālmīki said:
Know this mantra of Hanumān, which bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation, and which wards off great misfortunes, great sins, and all suffering. (2)
Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ! To Hanumān, the messenger of Rāma; to the destroyer of Laṅkā; to him born from the womb of Añjanā;
to the destroyer of Śākinīs and Ḍākinīs; to the one who causes the *kilikili* and *bhū-bhūkāra* sounds; to Vibhīṣaṇa.
Oṃ hrīṃ hrauṃ hrāṃ hrūṃ phaṭ svāhā to the divine Hanumān.
May all the sages know another mantra of Hanumān, known by the name "Sahasranāma," which destroys great calamities. (3)
By the mere remembrance of whom [Rāma] obtained Sītā and a kingdom free of thorns, and bestowed it upon Vibhīṣaṇa, just as he had regained his own self. || 4 ||
The sages said:
O Vālmīki, quickly tell us the excellent mantra of the Thousand Names, which wards off the flood of suffering and sin; we wish to hear this supreme narrative.
Vālmīki said:
"O all you sages, listen to this hymn of a thousand names,
the most excellent among hymns, divine, and the illuminator of the ultimate truth."
Of this great mantra, the *Śrī Hanumat Sahasranāmastotra*, Śrī Rāmacandra is the seer (*ṛṣi*),
Hanūmān is the deity (*devatā*), Anuṣṭubh is the meter (*chandaḥ*), Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ Hraḥ is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), Śrī is the power (*śakti*),
Kili-kili Bhrū Bhrū Kāreṇa is the pin (*kīlaka*), and Laṅkāvidhvaṃsanāya is the armor (*kavaca*).
The application (*viniyoga*) is for the purpose of pacifying all calamities and for the accomplishment of all desires during the recitation (*japa*).
Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Hanumān, the messenger of Rāma, with the two thumbs.
Salutation to the destroyer of Laṅkā, with the two index fingers.
Homage to the two middle fingers, born from the womb of Añjanā;
homage to the two ring fingers for the destruction of Śākinīs and Ḍākinīs;
Oṃ kili kili bhrū bhrū, homage to the god Hanumān, the terrifying one by his roar, with the two little fingers.
Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ hrāṃ phaṭ svāhā. Homage to both palms and backs of the hands. Oṃ to Hanumān, the messenger of Rāma, homage to the heart. To the destroyer of Laṅkā, homage to the head, svāhā.
Oṃ hrauṃ, to the tuft of hair (śikhā) born from the womb of Añjanā, vauṣaṭ!
Oṃ hrāṃ, for the destruction of Śākinīs and Ḍākinīs, to the armor (kavaca), hūṃ!
Oṃ kili kili bhrū bhrū, to the god Hanumān, who is terrifying by his roar, to the three eyes, vauṣaṭ!
Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ hrauṃ hrāṃ phaṭ svāhā | Phaṭ to the weapon (astra). Meditation: [One should meditate on the deity] possessing the luster of molten gold, with eyes reddish and crimson.
One should meditate upon him accompanied by Sugrīva and others, clothed in yellow garments.
He has turned the ocean into a mere puddle for a cow's hoofprint; he holds his tail and head as the Lord, bears the mudrā of knowledge, and is adorned with all ornaments.
One should meditate upon Hanumān, whose circle of faces is being pulled by his left hand, while his right arm is raised.
Hanumān, the bestower of prosperity, the son of Vāyu, Rudra, the leader, the ageless, the immortal, the hero of heroes, the dweller in the village, and the refuge of people. || 1 ||

The giver of wealth, whose form is beyond attributes, the hero, the lord of treasures, the sage, the tawny-eyed one, the granter of boons, the eloquent speaker, and the destroyer of Sītā’s sorrow. || 2 ||
Śiva, Śarva, the Supreme, the Unmanifest, the Manifest-Unmanifest, the Supporter of the Earth;
he with tawny hair and tawny body-hair, who is accessible through the Vedas, the Eternal One. (3)
The Lord is beginningless, divine, the cause of the universe, and the refuge of humanity;
he is the healer, the Lord of all, the Protector of the world, and the Sovereign of Hari.
Bharga, Rāma, the devotee of Rāma, the Lord of auspicious nature, the sustainer of the universe, the universal form, the one whose shape is the universe, and the protector of the universe. || 5 ||
The soul of the universe, the one to be served by the universe, the universe itself, the sustainer of the universe, the sun;
the activator of the universe, the one accessible to the universe, the one to be meditated upon by the universe, and the bearer of all arts. || 6 ||
The leaper, the best of monkeys, the eldest, the one to be known, the forest-dweller;
the child, the old man, the youth, the reality, the one accessible through reality, and indeed the unborn friend.
The son of Añjanā, unperturbed, is the mountain at the edge of the village;
he is Bhūr, Bhuvaḥ, Svar, Maharloka, Janaloka, and the imperishable Tapoloka. || 8 ||
He is Truth, accessible through the syllable Om, the all-pervading and stainless Praṇava;
he is the establisher of the dharma of Śiva, beloved by Rāma and dear to Phalguna.
He who has turned the lord of waters into mere hoofprints for his cattle, whose desires are fulfilled, the lord of the earth,
the slayer of demons, the lotus-eyed one, who is affectionate toward those who seek refuge.
The giver of life to Jānakī and the taker of the life of the Rākṣasa;
he is perfect, truthful, clad in yellow garments, and possesses a splendor equal to the sun. || 11 ||
The remover of Droṇa, the leader of Śakti, the slayer of the Rākṣasa Śakti, the destroyer of Akṣa, the messenger of Rāma, and the taker of the life of the Śākinīs. || 12 ||

He who has destroyed his enemies through the desire to enjoy [the world], the crusher of the mountain of pride, the cause yet causeless, the lofty one, the creator of the universe, and the teacher of the world. (13)
Lord of the world, leader of the world, Master of the universe, Sovereign of men;
Hari who dwells within the world, Lord of Śrī, and the crusher of Garuḍa’s pride. || 14 ||
The banner of Pārtha is the son of Vāyu, with a white tail and immeasurable luster;
he has Brahmā as his tail, the Supreme Brahman as his tail, and is the one who prepared the bricks for Rāma. || 15 ||
Accompanied by Sugrīva and others, he is the wise monkey, the lord of monkeys;
he is the one who abides for an eon, the long-lived, and the gracious Sadāśiva.
He is right-mindedness, the true goal, the bestower of enjoyment and liberation, and the giver of fame;
he is fame itself, the granter of renown, the ocean, the bestower of prosperity, and auspiciousness.
The God who traverses the ocean, the destroyer of the fear of saṃsāra, the binder of Vālin, the conqueror of the universe, and the one established in all things. || 18 ||
The enemy of Laṅkā, the personification of Time, the destroyer of the house of the Lord of Laṅkā;
the abode of all beings, Vāsudeva, Vasu, the Lord of the three worlds.
Kṛṣṇa is the embodiment of Śrī Rāma; he is the destroyer of the palaces of Laṅkā.
Kṛṣṇa is praised by Kṛṣṇa; he is the peaceful one, the bestower of peace, and the creator of the universe.
The enjoyer of all, the slayer of Māra, the celibate student, the one who has conquered his senses;
he who moves upward, the one with a tail, the one wearing a garland, and the one who struck down the Rākṣasas with his tail.
The heroic son of the Wind-god, the slayer of Māra, the bestower of victory;
he who grants auspiciousness to the world, the meritorious one, whose hearing and chanting bring merit. (22)
He is of meritorious fame and meritorious song, the purifier of the purifiers of the world; he is the Lord of Gods, possessed of infinite hair, and the ordainer of devotion to Rāma. || 23 ||
The meditator, the object of meditation, the witness of the world, the conscious one, whose very form is consciousness;
the giver of knowledge, the giver of life, the vital breath, the life-force of the universe, and the wind. || 24 ||
The beloved of Vibhīṣaṇa, the hero, the bestower of perfection upon those who take refuge in the Pippala tree;
the perfected one, the refuge of the perfected ones, Time itself, worshipped by the devourer of Time. || 25 ||
The Lord who dwells in the destruction of the Lord of Laṅkā, the burner of Laṅkā;
whose eyes are the moon, the sun, and fire; the fire of time that brings an end to the dissolution.
Kapila, Kapiśa, Puṇyarāti, he who dwells in the twelve zodiac signs, the refuge of all, the immeasurable self, and the one who wards off Revatī and the others. || 27 ||
The giver of life to Lakṣmaṇa, the cause of Sītā’s survival, the meditator on Rāma, Hṛṣīkeśa, the devotee of Viṣṇu, the one with matted hair, and the powerful one. (28)
He is the destroyer of the pride of the enemies of the gods, the invoker, the sustainer, the creator, and the Lord of the world;
he is the protector of cities and villages, pure, awakened, and without interval. || 29 ||
Stainless, free from conceptual construction, transcending the qualities (guṇas), and formidable;
Hanumān is difficult to propitiate, and Maheśvara is to be attained through austerity. || 30 ||
Parāśara is the remover of the intense heat arising from Jānakī’s grief;
he is the embodiment of speech, whose nature is both existent and non-existent, and the cause beyond primordial matter (prakṛti).
The bestower of fortune, the pure leader, the burner of Laṅkā; the Rākṣasa bound by his tail, who is dear to the enemies of the Rākṣasas. || 32 ||
The remover of shadows, the lord of beings, the lord of the worlds, the bestower of the good path;
the lord of monkeys, wrath, and he whose eyes are bloodshot with anger. (33)
The remover of anger, the remover of suffering, the bestower of fearlessness and boons upon his devotees;
he who is compassionate toward his devotees, the Lord of the Universe, the one invoked by many, the destroyer of cities. 34.
Agni, Vibhāvasu, Bhāsvat, Yama, Nirṛti, Varuṇa, Vāyugati, Vāyu, Kubera, and Īśvara; || 35 ||
The Sun, the Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, Rāhu, Ketu, Marud, Dātā, Dhātā, and Hartā born of the Wind. (36)
He who has turned the enemy of the gods into a mere mosquito; the enemy of the Daityas; the slayer of Madhu;
the god of love; the monkey; the protector of desire; the tawny one; and the life of the universe. || 37 ||
The lotus feet of Bhāgīrathī; expert in the construction of the bridge;
Svāhā, Svadhā, Havis, Kavya, and Havyavāha; the Illuminator. (38)
Self-luminous, the great hero, sweet, and of immeasurable valor;
possessing the flight of the soaring bird, the true refuge, the Supreme Person.

He is the soul of the world, the source of the world, and indeed the end of the world; he is without interior, free from evil, stainless, and great—the Great Principle (mahat) and the ego-sense (ahaṅkāra).
He is space, wind, earth, water, fire, the directions, time, and the one without a second;
he is the knower of the field (kṣetrajña) and the protector of the field (kṣetrapāla), who has turned the ocean into a mere puddle. || 41 ||
The golden one, the ancient, the sky-walker, the earth-walker, the Manu;
the Golden Embryo (Hiraṇyagarbha), the Thread-Self (Sūtrātman), the King of Kings, the Lord of the People.
He is the Udgītha known through the Vedānta, a limb of the Veda, and one who has reached the further shore of the Vedas;
he dwells in every village, is the immediate bestower of spiritual manifestation, and is a mine of virtues.
He is garlanded with stars, the soul of all beings, fragrant, and the wish-fulfilling tree;
he is the thought-gem, the treasury of virtues, and the unsurpassed gateway for all creatures.
The Lord of the Night, the enemy of Tripura, the wise one of meritorious fame,
caused the bhūtas, pretas, and piśācas to tremble with the sound of "kil-kila" cries.
He is the remover of the three debts, the subtle, the gross, the omnipresent Person;
he is the remover of epilepsy, the rememberer, the Veda, the song, the tradition, and Manu.
The Lord of Ascetics is the door to heaven, the door to progeny, and the door to liberation;
he is the Supreme Brahman in the form of Sound, the Brahman, the Ancient One of the City of Brahman.
The person is one and many, pure, self-luminous, and undisturbed;
he is light within light, beginningless, and characterized by the qualities of sattva, rajas, and tamas. 48.
The dispeller of darkness, the supportless, the formless, the mine of virtues;
the locus of qualities, consisting of qualities, of vast body, and of great fame.
He has a large bow, large feet, a large head, and a loud voice;
he has large ears, a large nose, large arms, and a large body.
He has a large throat, a large body, a large tail, and large hands;
he possesses great movement, is served by the great, and bestows the fruits of the vast worlds. || 51 ||
He who possesses vast devotion, who bestows the fruit of great desires, the Great Lord;
he who is praised by the vast world, the Seer, the giver of knowledge, and the Teacher of the Universe.
The preceptor of the gods, truthful in speech, a proponent of the Veda, and a master of the arts;
one who can travel to the seven netherworlds and who dwells on the Malaya mountain.
The Lord of Śrī situated in the northern quarter, the bird under the power of divine herbs,
the branch-monkey, the lord of apes, and the ancient one who delights in vital breath.
The Brahmin is the fourfold yogi, accessible to yogis, both supreme and inferior;
he is without beginning or end, the all-pervading Vyāsa, Vaikuṇṭha, and the Lord of the Earth.
The unconquered one, the conqueror of enemies, the eternal bestower of bliss, the Lord;
the protector of the earth, the lord of cattle, the warrior, the dark age, the plowshare, and the one higher than the highest. || 56 ||
He whose speed is the mind, ever-yoked, the destroyer of the fear of saṃsāra;
the giver of reality, the knower of reality, reality itself, and the illuminator of reality. (57)
Pure, awakened, eternally disciplined, the form of devotion, the chariot of the world;
he is dissolution, possessed of immeasurable illusion, yet transcending illusion and free from envy.
He is the protection won through illusion, the world created by illusion,
the refuge of illusion, the lord who brings illusion to an end, and he who is happy.
The Naga who is blissful and the bestower of bliss, praised by Maheśa; the Great Lord (Maheśvara) true to his promise, Śarabha, the purifier of the Kali age. || 60 ||
Taste is the knower of taste, honor is form, the eye is sound, the ear is smell, the nose is touch, and the sense of touch is indeed the *hiṅkāra* residing in the mind. (61)
He who is to be known as "not this, not this," who is fond of worshiping Vaikuṇṭha,
Giriśa, the beloved of Girijā, Durvāsas, Kavi, and Aṅgiras.
Bhṛgu, Vasiṣṭha, Cyavana, Nārada, Tumburu, Hara, Viśvakṣetra, Viśvabīja, Viśvanetra, and Viśvapa. (63)
He is the officiating priest and the sacrificer, the purifier and likewise the ancestors;
he is faith, intellect, forgiveness, and lassitude; he is the mantra, the one who recites the mantra, and the deity.
The lord of kings, the sovereign who has ascended [to power], the garlanded one, the charioteer of worldly existence;
he is eternal, his desires are ever fulfilled, and he is the supreme granter of the wishes of his devotees. (65)
He is the leader of the hosts, Keśava, the brother, the father, and the mother; he is the son of the Wind-god, possessing a thousand heads, a thousand mouths, a thousand eyes, and a thousand feet.
The conqueror of desire, the burner of desire, the embodiment of desire, the bestower of desirable fruits;
the remover of obstacles, the slayer of demons, the bearer of the earth’s burden, and the powerful one.
Armed with claws and fangs, he is a devotee of Viṣṇu who grants fearlessness to his devotees;
he is the destroyer of pride yet the giver of pride, possessing a hundred forms of fangs while remaining formless.
The great treasure, the highly fortunate one, the possessor of great splendor, the bestower of great supernatural power;
the one of great form, the great yogi, the one of great majesty, and the one of great radiance.
He is the one of great action, the one of great sound, the one of great mantra, and the one of great intelligence;
he is the one of great tranquility, the one of great magnanimity, the all-pervading Lord whose nature is Mahādeva.
Rudrakarman, Krūrakarman, Ratnanābha, Kṛtāgama, Ambhodhilaṅghana, Siddha, Satyadharman, and Pramodana. || 71 ||
Jitāmitra, Jaya, Soma, Vijaya, Vāyuvāhana, Jīva, Dhātṛ, Sahasrāṃśu, Mukunda, and Bhūridakṣiṇa. || 72 ||
He who has accomplished his purpose, the bestower of success, the perfected one, the resolve, the cause of attainment;
he whose feet traverse the seven netherworlds, and who is worshipped by the host of the seven seers.

The hero who has crossed the seven oceans, whose vast domain comprises the seven continents, who bestows the happiness of a kingdom with its seven constituents, and who is served by the seven mothers. (74)
He is the unique crown of the seven worlds, the performer of the sevenfold sacrifice, and the refuge of the sacred syllables;
he is praised by the seven Sāman chants and dwells within the seven netherworlds.
He is the treasury of the seven meters, the seven meters themselves, and the refuge of the seven classes of beings;
he bestows intelligence, bestows fame, removes sorrow, and destroys misfortune. (76)
It brings everything under control, removes defects of the womb, bestows sons and grandsons, paralyzes the mouths of opponents, and pacifies an angry mind. (77)
The pacifier of hostile sorcery, the destroyer of suffering, the giver of liberation from bondage;
the support of the city of nine gates, whose abode is the nine gates. || 78 ||
Praised by Nara and Nārāyaṇa, he is the Great Lord of the nine lords;
girt with a belt, clad in armor, and bearing a sword, he is resplendent and has Jiṣṇu as his charioteer.
His tail is many yojanas in width; with his tail he struck down asuras; he is the slayer of the wicked, the restrainer, and the destroyer of piśācas and grahas. || 80 ||
He is the destroyer of child-seizing spirits, the leader of the Dharma, and the source of compassion;
he is fierce in his deeds, fierce in his speed, fierce in his gaze, and the performer of a hundred sacrifices.

Praised by Śatamanyu, he is the one worthy of praise, the act of praise, the praiser, and possessed of great strength; he is endowed with all virtues, ever-active, and the destroyer of Rākṣasas. || 82 ||

The destroyer of demons, the forest-fire to the wicked, the Lord of Brahmā, the sustainer of prosperity, affectionate toward his devotees, the roar of the clouds, the embodiment of the cloud, and the warder-off of torrential rains. || 83 ||
He is the cause of life for the clouds, dark as a rain-cloud, and the supreme self; he is the son of the Wind, the Sustainer, and one who is proficient in the knowledge of the principles.

He is the unerring one, the one whose rain is never in vain, the giver of what is desired, and the destroyer of what is undesired; he is the purpose, the remover of misfortune, the capable one, and the servant of Rāma. || 85 ||
The seeker of truth, the blessed one, the enemy of the asuras, the lotus-eyed one, the self-born, Saṅkarṣaṇa, the pure-souled one, the mass of knowledge, and the lord of the gods. || 86 ||
The eternal uprooter of the immovable, the builder of the bridge, the charioteer of Rāma;
bliss, supreme bliss, the fish, the tortoise, the treasure, and the serpent.
Varāha, Nārasiṃha, Vāmana, Jamadagnija (Paraśurāma), Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, Śiva, Buddha, Kalki, and Hari who takes refuge in Rāma. 88.
Nandi, Bhṛṅgi, Caṇḍī, and Gaṇeśa, who is served by the hosts;
the presiding lord of karma, the delighter of the gods, the place of rest, and the sovereign of the world.
Jagannātha, Lord of Monkeys, Abode of All, Eternal Refuge; praised by Sugrīva and others, Self-controlled, Performer of All Deeds, the Leaper. || 90 ||
And Nakhadāritarakṣas, who is skilled in hand-to-hand combat with claws; likewise Sudhana, Śeṣa, Vāsuki, and Takṣaka are all proficient. (91)
Golden-hued and endowed with strength, the conqueror of cities and destroyer of sins;
the lamp of liberation, the embodiment of liberation, Garuḍa, the subduer of serpents, and the preceptor. || 92 ||

He who brings about the sound "klī-klī," the destroyer of pride through the removal of fear, the shatterer of mountains, whose limbs are like adamant, whose mouth is like adamant, and who wards off the adamantine obstacles of his devotees. || 93 ||

He whose weapons are his claws, who has a jeweled neck, who is garlanded with flames, and who is the sun; he of mature majesty, the scorcher, and the dispeller of the distress of his devotees. || 94 ||
He is the refuge, the life-force, and the enjoyer; he is characterized by various activities and is ever-fickle.
He is self-abiding, the destroyer of ill-health, the shatterer of suffering—the son of the Wind-god. (95)
The purifier, the wind, the beloved, he whose limbs are his devotees, the endurer, the powerful one;
the enemy of Meghanāda, who destroyed the Rākṣasa Meghanāda. || 96 ||
The perishable and the imperishable, the self-disciplined one, the lord of monkeys, the refuge of the virtuous;
Śrīkaṇṭha, the blue-throated one, the companion, and the leader together.
He is neither gross nor subtle; he is the splendor that destroys the cycle of worldly existence.
He is the essence of the science of the supreme self, skilled in the supreme self, and possessed of a wise intellect.
He is stainless, the cause of truth, the giver of truth, and whose sphere is truth;
he is the womb of truth, whose form is truth, truth itself, and whose prowess is truth.
He is the life-force of Añjanā, the Liṅga, born of the lineage of Vāyu, and the Revealed Scripture;
he is Bhadrarūpa, Rudrarūpa, Surūpa, and the bearer of Citrarūpa.
Saluted by Maināka, he is the seer of the subtle, the victorious, and the conqueror;
he has traversed the circle of the quarters, he is Rudra, whose prowess has been made manifest. || 101 ||
Conch-necked, serene-souled, with a short nose and a large belly,
he had hanging lips, wore earrings, and was adorned with a variegated garland— the best among those who know yoga.
He is the wise seer, whose form is bliss, the destroyer of no small [suffering],
the son of Phālgunī, undisturbed, whose self is yoga, and who is intent upon yoga.
He is the knower of yoga, the performer of yoga, the source of yoga, and the sky-clad one;
his body is fashioned from the letters beginning with 'a' and ending with 'kṣa'. || 104 ||
The Supreme Lord has a mouth like a mortar, is praised by the Siddhas, has joined shanks, joined knees, joined palms, and wears a topknot. || 105 ||
Suśarman, Amitadharman, and Nārāyaṇaparāyaṇa;
Jiṣṇu, Bhaviṣṇu, Rociṣṇu, Grasiṣṇu, and Sthāṇu. (106)
The tawny one, the imitator of Rudra, the shaker of trees, the shaker of the earth, the flow of qualities, the self of the thread, the one free from passion, and the lover of praise. || 107 ||
He is the destroyer of the fear of the Naga maidens, the one who has fulfilled all that was to be done, and the bearer of the skull-cup;
he is favorable, imperishable, free from calamity, beyond all misfortune, and one who has reached the further shore of the Vedas.
The imperishable Puruṣa, the Lord of the world, the three-eyed, the sovereign, the firm one;
the fruit of the eightfold yoga, the one true to his promise, the one praised by many. || 109 ||

His abode is the cremation ground; he is capable of putting to flight the hungry ghosts (preta); he is devoted to the five-syllable mantra; he is the banner of the five Mothers; he is the one who delights. 110.
His glory is worshipped by the assembly of Yoginīs; he is the slayer of enemies and possesses infinite valor.
He is a celibate student whose body consists of the senses, who wields the staff of discipline, and who is composed of the ten [organs]. (111)
Aprapañca, Sadācāra, Śūrasena, Vidāraka, Buddha, Pramoda, Ānanda, Saptajihvapati, and Dhara. || 112 ||
The support of the city of nine gates, ever fresh, the singer of the Sāman hymns;
the abode of the six chakras, the remover of fear from the heavenly world, the bestower of honor, and intoxication itself. 113.
He who brings all under his control, the power, the infinite one, the possessor of infinite auspiciousness;
the bearer of the eight forms, the leader, the multiformed, and the one beautiful by his own nature.
Dhūmaketu, Mahāketu, Satyaketu, Mahāratha, Nandīpriya, Svatantra, Mekhalī, and Ḍamarupriya. || 115 ||
Lohitāṅga, Samidvahnī, Ṣaḍṛtu, Śarva, Īśvara, Phalabhuk, Phalahasta, and the bestower of the fruits of all actions. || 116 ||
He is the overseer of dharma, the fruit of dharma, dharma itself, the bestower of dharma, and the giver of wealth;
he is the knower of the twenty-five principles, the savior, and one who is intent upon the reality of Brahman.
He who dwells upon the three paths, the formidable one, the destroyer of all that is wicked;
the Lord of Vitality, the Lord of Waters, the wielder of the trident, the wearer of the garland, and the maker of night. 118.
Clad in red garments, red in hue, adorned with red garlands, wearing a forest garland, with auspicious limbs, white, dressed in white robes, and youthful. 119.
Victory belongs to him whose retinue is invincible, who has a thousand faces, and who is the Seer;
he is the shatterer of Śākinīs, Ḍākinīs, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, and Bhūtas.
Sadyojāta, Kāmagati, Jñānamūrti, Yaśaskara, Śambhutejas, Sārvabhauma, Viṣṇubhakta, and Plavaṅgama. || 121 ||
He is the knower of the ninety-four mantras, the destroyer of the pride of Rāvaṇa’s strength, the bestower of all prosperity, the illustrious one, and the increaser of the joy of Aṅgada. 122.
The Lord of the Gods is the seed of mindfulness, the destroyer of the fear of saṃsāra;
he is the supreme Śrīparīvāra, Śrībhū, Ugra, and the fulfiller of desires.
He whose movement is constant, who is the wind, who is a bee at the lotus-feet of Rāma;
he who loves the color blue, who is blue in color, and who is a friend dear to those of blue hue. 124.
The messenger of Rāma, the friend of the world, the inner self, and the enchanting one; the hero who practices meditation on Śrī Rāma, who is always praised by the Kimpuruṣas. 125.
He is the intimate confidant of Rāma’s mission, pure, free from all affliction,
renowned for his virtuous fame, supreme bliss, and the beloved charioteer of the Supreme Lord.
The Lord of the world, the giver of liberation, the cause of all causes,
the one of great strength, the great hero, the teacher who has reached the further shore beyond the ocean.
The Blessed One is the savior, the protector, the bestower of well-being, and the source of auspiciousness;
he is the witness of all worlds and is worshipped by all the gods;
he is the bearer of the burden of service at the feet of Śrī Rāma, who is endowed with the glory of the Arhats. || 128 ||
The man who studies this thousand names every day quickly destroys the flood of suffering, and his prosperity increases for a long time;
the fourfold subjugation comes to him without a doubt. (129)
Kings, princes, and royal ministers are seen [to attain their goals] within three fortnights by reciting this at the three times of day. (130)
For those who recite it at the foot of an aśvattha tree, there is no fear caused by enemies;
by reciting this at the three times of day, accomplishment shall be held in the palm of one's hand.
The man who rises during the Brāhma-muhūrta and recites this every day obtains both worldly and otherworldly benefits; of this there is no doubt. (132)
For those stationed in battle, it shall bring about the routing of enemies;
it pacifies fevers and epilepsy, and wards off diseases such as abdominal tumors (gulma).
For those men who recite this— which bestows the wealth and happiness of universal sovereignty—
he who reads it daily or causes it to be read with a concentrated mind attains all desires through the grace of the Son of the Wind (Hanumān). 134.
The *Śrī Āñjaneya-sahasranāmastotra* and the *Hanumat-sahasranāmastotra* are complete.
